reading.rtitle: NatureCare Skin -- Partner Wanted: Exclusive Representative for Brazil
paras: NatureCare Skin is a family brand from Boston. We make sunscreen and face creams for sensitive skin, and we sell them in pharmacies in the United States and Mexico. Now we want to expand to Brazil, and we are looking for a representative.

What does our representative do? The representative sells our products to pharmacy chains and to distributors. The representative does not have to buy the products: the distributor buys them and takes them to the pharmacies. But the representative has to visit the buyers, show our catalog and find a good place on the shelf.

The agreement is for two years, and it is exclusive: you represent NatureCare in Brazil, and we do not work with other representatives there. In year one, your territory is the state of Sao Paulo. From year two, it is all of Brazil.
You do not have to pay anything to start. You receive a commission of eight percent on every sale. We send free samples and catalogs, and we pay for your trip to Boston for training.

What do you have to bring? Experience in pharmacy retail, good contacts with pharmacy chains, and good English for our calls. Do you have to speak Spanish? No, you don't. You have to send us your plan by June thirtieth.

listenings.text: Hi Gleice, this is Jennifer Lowe, the sales director of NatureCare Skin. Thank you for your interest in our partner page. I want to explain the job before our call. First, you don't have to be an employee of NatureCare. You work for yourself, and you receive a commission on every sale. We pay the commission every three months. Second, you have to visit at least twenty buyers every month, in pharmacy chains and distributors. Third, you have to send a short report about your visits every Friday. It is only one page. And finally, in September you have to come to Boston for one week of training. Don't worry, you don't have to pay for the trip. We pay for everything. Talk to you soon.

I have worked as a brand representative in pharmacies for fifteen years, and here is my advice. Before you sign an agreement, read it slowly, and check three things: the territory, the commission, and if it is exclusive. You don't have to accept the first offer. You can ask for a bigger territory or a better commission. Brands expect that. Then, when you start, remember one thing: the shelf is everything. If your product is not on the shelf at eye level, nobody buys it. So you have to visit the stores, not only the offices. And always take the catalog with you. Buyers have to see the products.

extra_audio.text: First, NatureCare says it wants to expand to Brazil. Then it explains that the distributor buys the products. After that, it says the agreement is exclusive for two years. Next, it says the representative receives a commission of eight percent. Finally, it says you have to send your plan by June thirtieth.
